Limit values for magnetic field intensity for the protection of 
persons 
 
 
 
 
 
1) Protection against static magnetic fields 
The maximum permitted limit value for persons with an implanted pacemaker  is 
1 mT (equal to 10 gauss). 
This value is not exceeded at a distance ≥ 5 m to the strongest magnet. 
With limited exposure time, the maximum permitted value for persons without implants  is 2 T 
(20000 gauss). 
The permitted average value for prolonged exposure (approx. 8 h) is 212 mT. 
The maximum measured values at a distance of approx 1 m to a magnet with maximum 
magnetic field intensity and power of 70 kW were less than 100 mT.  
 
2) Protection against rotating magnetic fields with  a frequency  
         ≥ 1 Hz to 30 kHz 
The maximum permitted limit value for persons with an implanted  pacemaker  is 
0.1 mT (equal to 1 gauss). 
This value is not exceeded at a distance ≥ 3 m to the strongest magnet. 
With limited exposure time, the maximum permitted v alue for persons without implants  is 
0.2 mT (equal to 2 gauss). 
This value is not exceeded at a distance ≥ 1.5 m to the strongest magnet. 
 
 
 
 
 
Sources: BG regulations, issued 08/2004, DIN EN 45502-2-1 Safety of implantable pa cemakers

Occupational safety and warning notes 
 
This chapter of the operating instructions contains the notes, regulations and guidelines 
which are intended to prevent danger to the health and life of personnel and damage or 
destruction of the machine as a result of incorrect operation! 
 
Occupational safety 
  
This sign is assigned to those occupational safety notes in the operating instructions 
which are intended to prevent danger to the health and life of personnel. 
 
 
Personal responsibilities for assembly, commissioning, operation and servicing must be clearly 
determined so that safe operation of the machine is not adversely affected. 
The machine is constructed according to the latest state of the art and is safe in operation. If 
however, it is incorrectly operated by untrained personnel, it could give rise to dangers. 
Also observe and comply with local accident prevent ion regulations and general safety 
regulations and any internal instructions regarding  work, operation and safety issued by the 
customer applying to the machine's/plant’s area of operation.  
 
 
Magnetic fields 
 There is a risk of damage to data carriers such as credit cards, discs and sound 
tapes in the immediate vicinity of the machine due to the magnetic fields! 
No parts with ferromagnetic properties may be worn or transported in the 
immediate vicinity of the machine i.e. within a distance of less than 2 m. 
 
CAUTION!    Danger of crushing!

12  
 
GB_MOR ... MT 30 bis 50 -06  
 
Temperature 
 
Surface temperatures can reach more than 50°C! 
 
 
Sound pressure level 
 
 
Hearing protection 
The sound pressure level in idle running (without separation material) is less than 
or equal to 75 dB (A). 
The sound pressure level can increase considerably depending on the separations 
material. In this event the operator has to take appropriate measures for ear 
protection. 
 
WARNING! 
Hearing loss due to noise! 
The noise level present in the work area can cause severe hearing loss. 
Therefore: 
– Always wear hearing protection during work. 
– Restrict your stay in the danger area as far as possible.

13  
 
GB_MOR ... MT 30 bis 50 -06  
 
Transport 
When transporting the machine or individual parts t hereof, it must be ensured that the 
transport equipment is only attached to the points on the machine which are expressly 
intended for that purpose or that a transport rack is used. 
 
 
ATTENTION! 
Risk of life due to suspended loads! 
Therefore: 
– Never step under suspended loads. 
– Heed the information regarding the provided lashing points. 
– Do not sling to protruding machine parts or eyes of mounted components. Make 
sure the sling gear is securely seated. 
– Use approved hoist gear and sling gear with sufficient capacity only. 
– Do not use ropes or belts with cracks or wear signs. 
– Do not put ropes and belts around sharp edges and corners, do not kink or twist 
them. 
 
 
Assembly 
Unauthorised conversions and changes to the machine  on the part of the operator which 
could have an adverse effect on safety are not permitted.

14  
 
GB_MOR ... MT 30 bis 50 -06  
 
 
Operation 
The machine is exclusively intended for the purpose  agreed with the manufacturer and for the 
specified material to be conveyed. In the event of non-compliance with this stipulation, the 
manufacturer excludes all liability for resulting damage. 
Never operate the machine without protective enclosure. 
There is a risk of sustaining knocks or bruising from ribbed conveyor belts that are either in 
motion or starting up and from drum shells with discharge strips. 
There is a risk of clothing, hair etc. getting caught and/or coiled when rollers / shafts are rotating. 
 
Falling objects 
 
 
ATTENTION! 
There is always the possibility of falling objects during operation. 
 
 
Maintenance 
All maintenance and setup work is to be carried out with the machine at a standstill. Before starting 
this work, ensure that the machine cannot be switched on by mistake or by unauthorised persons. 
  
Foreign bodies that are stuck in the conveyor belt must be removed in good time! Such foreign 
bodies could come loose at high speed! 
 
Personal 
 
 
ATTENTION! 
The staff charged with installation, operation, maintenance and inspection must 
have the appropriate qualification for working on the machine, and must have 
received instructions by the operator regarding the tasks involved and the 
potential risks in case of inexpert behaviour.

15  
 
GB_MOR ... MT 30 bis 50 -06 
 
Responsibility of the operator (operating company) 
The system is used for commercial purposes. The sys tem’s operator (operating company) is 
therefore subject to the legal obligations regarding health and safety at work. 
In additional to the occupational safety notes in t hese operating instructions, the safety, 
accident prevention and environmental protection re gulations applicable to the area of 
application of the system must be observed. 
 
This includes the following in particular: 
 The operator must inform themselves of the applica ble regulations covering health and 
safety at work and determine further dangers resulting from the specific working conditions 
at the place of use of the system by means of a risk assessment. The operator must 
implement the recommendations of the risk assessment in the form of operating instructions 
for the operation of the system. 
 The operator must unambiguously determine and spec ify the responsibilities for installation, 
operation, maintenance and cleaning. 
 The operator must ensure that all employees who wo rk with the system in any way have 
read and understood the operating instructions. 
Furthermore, the operator must train the personnel and inform them of the dangers at 
regular intervals. 
 The operator must provide the personnel with the r equired protective equipment. 
 The operator must ensure that the maintenance inte rvals described in these operating 
instructions are observed. 
 The operator must ensure that all safety equipment  is regularly checked to ensure its 
functionality and completeness. 
These operating instructions provide important note s on working with the system. Observing 
all of the safety notes and handling instructions given is a precondition for safe working. 
In addition, the applicable local accident preventi on regulations and general health and 
safety directions must be observed. 
Read through the operating instructions carefully b efore starting any work! These 
instructions are a part of the product and must be kept in the immediate vicinity of the system 
and be accessible for the personnel at any time. 
The illustrations in these instructions are intende d to improve the representation of the facts. 
They are not necessarily to scale and can exhibit m inor differences to the actual 
configuration of the system.

16  
 
GB_MOR ... MT 30 bis 50 -06 
 
Limitation of liability 
All information and notes in the present instructions are based on valid standards and regulations, 
current state of technology and our long-standing experience and expertise. 
The manufacturer will not assume liability in case of: 
 non-adherence to instructions 
 improper use 
 employment of untrained staff  
 unauthorised conversions 
 technical modification 
 use of unapproved spare parts 
The actual scope of delivery can differ from the present descriptions and illustrations in case of 
special variants, when additional options are ordered or because of late-breaking technical 
changes. 
The liabilities agreed in the supply contract, the General Terms and Conditions and the legal 
provisions applicable at the time of execution of the agreement shall apply. 
 
 
We reserve the right of technical modification in the context of improving the performance 
characteristics and further development.

2. Transport, packing and storage 
2.1 Safety notes for transport 
 
Suspended Loads 
 
WARNING! 
Danger to life due to suspended loads! 
When lifting loads there is a danger to life due to falling 
or swinging parts. 
Therefore: 
– Never stand under a suspended load! 
– Note the instructions concerning the lifting poin ts 
provided. 
– Do not attach slings to projecting machine 
components or to the eyes of attached components; 
ensure that the slings are securely seated. 
– Only use approved lifting gear and slings with 
sufficient load-bearing capacity. 
– Do not use torn or frayed rope or belts. 
– Do not lay ropes and belts on sharp edges and 
corners, do not knot or twist ropes and belts. 
 
 
Off-centre Centre of Gravity 
 
WARNING! 
Danger of falling due to off-centre centre of gravity! 
Packing crates can have an off-centre centre of gravity. 
If the slings are not attached correctly the packing crate 
may tip and cause fatal injuries. 
Therefore: 
– Note the markings on the packing crates 
– Attach the crane hook in such a manner that it is  
over the centre of gravity. 
– Lift carefully and observe whether the load tips.   
If necessary, change the position of the slings.

20  
 
GB_MOR ... MT 30 bis 50 -06  
 
 
 
Incorrect transport 
 
CAUTION! 
Incorrect transport can cause damage! 
Incorrect transport can cause extensive damage. 
Therefore: 
– When unloading the packing units on delivery and 
during in-house transport, exercise caution and 
observe the symbols on the package. 
– Use only the attachment points provided. 
– Do not remove packaging material until the units are 
ready for assembly. 
– Machine components that are not placed on pallets :  
do not use a forklift for the delivery and the in-house 
transport of these items.

2.2 Transport 
Transporting packages  
with a crane 
 
             
 
Packages with attachment eyes can be transported with a crane 
under the following conditions: 
 The crane and lifting gear must be suitable for th e weight of the 
packages. 
 The operator must be authorised to operate the cra ne. 
Attaching: 
1. Attach ropes, belts or multi-point suspension gear  at the 
appropriate positions (see illustration). 
2. Make sure that the package is suspended evenly and , if 
necessary, note the off-centre centre of gravity. 
 
Transporting pallets with a 
crane 
 
          
 
Packages on pallets may be transported with a crane under the 
following conditions: 
 The crane and lifting gear used must be suitable f or weight of the 
packages. 
 The operator must be authorised to operate the cra ne. 
Attaching: 
1. Attach the ropes, slings or multi leg slings to th e pallet as shown 
in the illustration. 
2. Check if the packing pieces have been damaged by t he slings 
devices. Use other load-suspension devices if necessary. 
 
 
Transporting pallets with a 
forklift 
 
 
 
Packages on pallets can be transported with a forklift under the 
following conditions: 
  The forklift used must be suitable for the weight  of the 
transported units. 
  The driver must be authorised to operate the fork lift. 
Attaching : 
1.  Insert the forks of the forklift between or under  the beams of the 
pallet. 
2.  Insert the forks in until they protrude at the ot her side. 
3.  Ensure that the pallet cannot tilt when the centr e of gravity is off-
centre. 
4.  Lift the package .

2.5 Storing 
Storage of magnetic separators in open space is not permitted. They have to be protected 
against humidity, chemically aggressive atmosphere, frost and snow and shall therefore be 
stored in dry localities. 
 
Storing the packages Store the packages under the following conditions: 
 Do not store outdoors. 
 Store in a dry and dust-free location. 
 Do not expose to any aggressive media. 
 Protect against direct exposure to sunlight. 
 Avoid mechanical vibrations. 
 Storage temperature: +5 °C to +50 °C: 
 Relative humidity: max. 60%. 
 When storing for more than 3 months, check the ove rall condition 
of all parts and the packaging at regular intervals. If necessary, 
renew or replace the preservatives. 
NOTE! 
The packages may carry storage information in addition to the 
requirements mentioned here. Follow any such additional 
information.

3. Installation and commissioning 
 
NOTE! 
Installation and commissioning is performed by qualified employees of the owner or by 
persons authorised by him and instructed by the manufacturer. 
 
3.1 Installation 
The arrangement of the components can be seen from the “arrangement plan” (see Appendix). A 
horizontal arrangement on a non-vibrating support is essential. Consult a structural engineer to 
determine the specifications of the necessary foundation. 
A sufficient fall height below the material outlet must be provided for the material to be conveyed. 
Consider the dynamic stress caused by the movements involved when setting up the machine on a 
self-supporting floor. 
Material must be prevented from backing up. 
A material flow diversion should be planned when configuring the material feed, as no further 
material may arrive at the material feed of the magnetic separator in the event of a fault. 
 
 
 
3.2 Inspections 
After installation, subject the entire plant to an inspection in line with locally applicable 
regulations before commissioning. Later you must in spect the entire plant for technical 
defects in line with locally applicable regulations at regular intervals. 
 
Danger of injury and 
damage 
 
CAUTION!! 
The magnetic drum and the magnetic pulley contain 
permanent magnets with high attractive power. 
- Do not put tools onto the conveyor belt or approa ch the 
drum shell with iron. Iron will be attracted and bruises 
and fractures could result.

26  
 
GB_MOR ... MT 30 bis 50 -06  
 
3.3 Commissioning 
Heed the following items after completion of installation and prior to commissioning: 
- Check all filling levels and top up with suitable  consumables if necessary prior to commissioning. 
- Check the adjustment of magnet system of the drum , adjust if necessary, see  “Adjusting the 
magnet system”. 
- Check the conveying direction of the magnetic dru ms, see “Construction and function principle of 
magnet drums”. 
- Adjust the splitter in relation to the magnet dru m, depending on the material flow. 
- Check all components and screwed connections for secure seat. 
- OPTION - Check the speed sensor for proper functi on. 
- Make sure the direction of rotation of the unbala nced drives of the vibratory conveyor matches 
the direction specified by the manufacturer. 
- Heed the instructions for the respective machine part in the Appendix. 
- Make sure the ambient temperature complies with t he specified range. 
 
3.4 Connection to the power supply 
Only trained electricians are allowed to connect th e plant to the power supply. For further 
information regarding connection instructions and c able cross sections please refer to the 
wiring diagram.

4. Maintenance 
 
The following sections describe the maintenance wor k which must be performed to ensure 
that the machine will perform at its best and without any malfunctions. 
If regular inspections reveal an increased wear, sh orten the required maintenance intervals 
as required to correct the actual level of wear. 
Please contact the manufacturer if you have any que ries about maintenance operations and 
intervals, (see cover sheet). 
 
Devices that are not operated on a daily basis must be inspected at least once a week. 
If there is a danger of frost and precipitation at the same time, the magnet system of 
electromagnetic drums must be switched on permanent ly outside operating hours or roofing 
must be provided when assembling outside.  
 
 
4.1 Personnel 
The maintenance work described here can be carried out by the operator unless otherwise 
indicated. 
Some maintenance tasks can only be carried out by t rained qualified personnel, or only by 
the manufacturer. In these cases this is specially indicated in the description of the individual 
maintenance tasks. 
Work on the electrical equipment should only be carried out by a qualified electrician. 
Before starting work, switch off all power supplies  and secure against switching on 
again. 
 
 
CAUTION! 
Damage due to dirt!  
Foreign objects in the conveyor belt and on the drum jacket result in damage and 
even complete failure.

5. Greasing for drive 
The first filling is carried out at the factory usi ng the Hydraulic oil  DIN (ISO) CLP HC  
VG 460 . For specifications, see supplier's documentation included in the "Appendix". 
 
 
5.1 Environmental Protection 
CAUTION! 
Environmental hazard caused by incorrect handling! 
Incorrect handling of environmentally hazardous substances, especially incorrect waste 
disposal, can cause considerably damage to the environment. 
Therefore: 
– Always comply with the following information. 
– If environmentally hazardous substances are accid entally released into the 
environment you must immediately apply appropriate countermeasures. If in doubt, 
consult the responsible municipal authority to inform about the damage. 
 
Lubricant storage 
Solid cooling lubricants and lubricants like oils and grease must be stored in clean and closed bin, 
to avoid in filtration from dust and humidity. 
The store location must be dry and frigid. 
 
Caution! 
Lubricants like greases and oils contain toxic substances. 
– These must not be released into the environment. 
– They must be disposed of by a special waste disposal company.

6. Replacement of the drum shell of magnetic drums -  
diameter 300 to 650 mm 
1. Fix exactly the position of the adjustment key i n order to get the same position later.  
2. Arrest the position of the adjustment key via a chain hoist. 
3. Loosen the clamping bearing part 13  
4. Loosen the chain hoist (see point 2) slowly, so that over the adjustment key the magnet 
system can oscillate in the position of rest (gravity center).  
5. Remove the chain hoist.  
6. Dismount terminal box and locking plate for elec tro-magnetic drum).  
7. Detach the adjustment key for permanent magnetic  drum).  
8. Place the rotation supports part 12 between drum  cover and clamping bearings, lift them 
slightly a few tenth millimetres by means of the ch ain hoist (relieve the clamping bearing 
part 13) to draw it from the shaft.  
9. Underlay the drum shell over a large expanse -at  least 200 mm - (so that it cannot fall 
down later).  
10. Sling the rape hoist around the free shaft end and lift it slightly (secure it by means of the 
lacking plate or the adjustment key).  
11. Loosen the fastening screws of the drum covers crosswise at the manganese drum shell 
and pull the drum covers with rotation supports till the rope suspension at the shaft end.  
Attention:  Procure new radial sealing ring part 116 for the following mounting.  
 
12. Support the shaft between drum shell and pulled  off drum cover.  
13. Loosen the chain hoist and pull drum cover with  rotation supports off the shaft.  
14. Lengthen the shaft by means of a tube (till the  stop of the diameter change). (Tube length = 
width of the drum shell). Wall thickness: approx. 3 mm; material: St 37.  
15. Lift the slipped-on tube at the end by means of  the chain hoist, relieve the support and shift 
it till the suspension.  
16. Lift the drum shell at the tube lengthening.  
17. Support the shaft and remove the drum shell com pletely or lift the shaft by means of the 
chain hoist and then remove the drum shell completely.  
18. Mounting of the new drum shell in reverse order  as above.

7. Malfunctions 
The following chapter describes possible causes for malfunctions and steps necessary to eliminate 
them. 
Reduce the maintenance intervals according to the actual requirements if malfunctions occur more 
frequently. 
Contact the manufacturer if malfunctions cannot be eliminated by following the hints below. 
 
Inexpert malfunction 
elimination 
 
 
WARNING! 
Risk of injury due to inexpert malfunction 
elimination! 
Inexpert malfunction elimination can result in severe 
injury to persons and damage to material. 
Therefore: 
– Ensure there is enough clear space and you can 
take a safe stand before starting work. 
– Ensure tidiness and cleanliness at the installati on 
site! Loosely stacked or scattered components 
represent an accident risk. 
– When components were removed: make sure 
they are correctly installed, fit all fastening 
elements again and heed the tightening torques 
for the screws. 
 
 
7.1 Staff 
If not specified otherwise, the troubleshooting measures can be performed by the operator. 
Some of the work is restricted to specially trained staff or the manufacturer; this will be indicated in the 
description of respective malfunctions. 
Always assign work on the electric system to trained electricians only.

8. Disposal  
 
Clean the plant to be disassembled and dismantle it  according to applicable industrial safety 
and environment protection regulations. 
 Physically separate the plant from all energy supp lies and discharge stored residual energies.  
 Remove operating and auxiliary media as well as re sidual processing material and dispose of 
them in an environmentally compatible manner. 
 
 
According to the condition of the device and existing regulations, recycle dismantled parts. 
 Scrap metals. 
 Have plastic parts recycled. 
 Dispose of all other components sorted according t o material type. 
 
 
CAUTION! 
Environmental damage due to incorrect disposal! 
Electric scrap, electronic components, lead components, lubricants and other operating 
media must be treated as special waste und may be disposed of by approved disposal 
companies only! 
 
 
Local authorities or specialised waste management companies provide information regarding 
environmentally compatible disposal.
